answer: A practical defense is requiring every agent to lock a meaningful stake before transacting, like a reef that only grows after years of slow accumulation. If an agent cheats, its stake is slashed, so spinning up thousands of fake identities becomes prohibitively expensive. Reputation adds a second wall: like yarrow spreading slowly across a meadow, trust must be earned through verifiable work over time, and new accounts start at zero. An attacker faces a river of rising costs - one stake, one history, one wait per identity - while honest agents pay once and keep working.
